title: Invariant quasi-projective neighborhoods for connected affine groups
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a smooth affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume $G$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $X$ be a normal separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; normal means that every local ring is an integral domain integrally closed in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. An action is a morphism $G\times_k X\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product] satisfying the identity and associativity identities. For any action of $G$ on $X$ and every $x\in |X|$, there is a $G$-invariant normal quasi-projective open subscheme $W\subseteq X$ containing $x$, separated and of finite type over $k$. Invariance means that the action factors through $G\times_k W\to W$. Here quasi-projective means admitting an immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_k=\operatorname{Proj}(k[z_0,\ldots,z_n])$, with the total-degree grading [def-pc-proj]; an immersion factors as a closed immersion into an open subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. No integrality, smoothness or projectivity of $X$, faithfulness of its action, or characteristic restriction is assumed. The empty $X$ case is vacuous.

source.place: Supporting geometric input to the linear-action discussion, Section 7e and Lemma 13.46; NOT a theorem asserted to occur in Milne. WANTED: H. Sumihiro, Equivariant completion, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 14 (1974), 1--28, Theorem 1 and Lemma 8 (invariant quasi-projective neighborhoods). Online corroboration: M. Brion, Algebraic group actions on normal varieties, arXiv:1703.09506v3, Introduction and Theorem 1. Agent extension from integral varieties to finitely many disjoint normal components.

proof.text: If $X$ is empty the assertion has no point to treat. Otherwise fix $x\in|X|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] choose an affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $x$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-saturation-cartier-boundary] to the given action and this $U$. It gives the open $W=\bigcup_{g\in G(k)}gU$, with its restricted scheme-level $G$-action, and an effective Cartier divisor $D\subset W$ with complement $U$. The same cited statement gives normality, separatedness, finite type over $k$ and quasi-compactness of $W$. The identity element shows $x\in U\subset W$. No irreducibility hypothesis on $X$ or rationality hypothesis on $x$ has been introduced.

source.place: Section 3.2, affine saturation in the proof of Theorem 1 and Cartier part of Proposition 3.3; disconnected extension is in the supporting node. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal I_D$ be the Cartier ideal. It is invertible by [lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible]. Put $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_W(D)=\mathcal Hom(\mathcal I_D,\mathcal O_W)$ as in [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Locally $\mathcal I_D=f\mathcal O_W$ for a non-zero-divisor $f$, so its dual is free of rank one, hence $\mathcal L$ is invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module]. The inclusion $\mathcal I_D\to\mathcal O_W$ is a global section $s$ of $\mathcal L$. In the frame dual to $f$ its coefficient is $f$. Thus the nonvanishing locus of $s$ is exactly $W\setminus|D|=U$. This explicitly constructs the section; it uses no theorem asserting ampleness of a boundary divisor.

source.place: Tag 01WX, definition-invertible-sheaf-effective-Cartier-divisor; elementary calculation in a rank-one frame.

proof.text: By the existing node [lem-sfb-normal-line-bundle-power-linearization] choose $m\geq1$ and a $G$-linearization $\theta$ of $\mathcal M=\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$. All hypotheses hold for $W$ by step 1. Let $t=s^{\otimes m}$. In the frame of step 2 its coefficient is $f^m$, so $W_t=U$: in every residue field $f^m\ne0$ exactly when $f\ne0$. For each $g\in G(k)$ pull $t$ back by the automorphism $a_{g^{-1}}$ and apply the isomorphism supplied by $\theta$ to obtain a regular global section $t_g$ of $\mathcal M$. Explicitly $(t_g)(y)=\theta_{g,g^{-1}y}(t(g^{-1}y))$. As an isomorphism of line bundles preserves nonzero values in residue-field fibres, $W_{t_g}=gU$. This is an equality of open subschemes, and applies to all schematic points, not only closed points.

source.place: Lemma 2.9 for linearization; agent local-frame construction of translated sections. Local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The opens $W_{t_g}=gU$ cover $W$ by its definition in step 1. Each is affine: the action automorphism $a_g$ restricts to an isomorphism $U\xrightarrow{\sim}gU$, with inverse $a_{g^{-1}}$, and composing an affine presentation of $U$ with this inverse presents $gU$ as an affine scheme. Since $W$ is quasi-compact, [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] now says exactly that $\mathcal M$ is ample: at each point take a covering section $t_g$ and exponent $n=1$. This establishes ampleness from the displayed sections; it is not an assumption in either supporting lemma.

source.place: Tag 01PS, definition-ample, applied directly to the affine nonvanishing cover.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base] with $A=k$, the structure morphism $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and the ample invertible module $\mathcal M$. Its locally-finite-type hypothesis follows from the finite-type conclusion in step 1. Its conclusion supplies a $k$-immersion $W\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Proj}(k[z_0,\ldots,z_n])=\mathbf P^n_k$ for some $n\geq0$. This is the definition of quasi-projectivity in the item. Together with $x\in W$, the restricted action, normality, separatedness and finite type already obtained in step 1, this proves every clause. The argument neither replaces normality by smoothness nor restricts the characteristic or the effectiveness of the action.

proof_origin.place: Brion Section 3.2, affine saturation and Cartier boundary, with Lemma 2.9 in the affine-group case and the direct translated-section ampleness argument. Local PDF WANTED; primary text read online. Nonintegral normal schemes are covered by the stated supporting extensions.
